To investigate the clumpy nature of the intra-cluster medium, researchers are analyzing second-order structure functions of bright X-ray lines. However, before studying XRM XIFU data, a thorough examination of the measurement process is necessary. This study uses synthetic data generated from a specific model to test the structure function method. It reveals that noise and limited data length result in biased estimates, making it difficult to determine the contributions of each factor. As a guide for upcoming experiments, a revised formula is proposed to account for data length effects and provide reliable confidence intervals for structure function estimates.

A graph factor R will be called Ramsey upper rich if it contains a subgraph r that also has the property of being an r-Kneser graph. It is already established that (2k-1)-colorable graph factors always have an subgraph r-Kneser graph r with no more than 2 roots, for all 2 roots 2k-1, where k is at least 3, but this result relies on the assumption that the number of vertices is sufficiently large. This study aims to replace the requirement of a large number of vertices with a condition of a certain type of graph. It is proven that if a graph has the property of being cyclically four-connecte, then it contains a factor R, regardless of the number of vertices; additionally, it is shown that graph factors two-colorable r-Kneser graphs always contain subgraphs two-colorable r-Kneser graphs with no more than 2 roots.

We developed a novel statistical method to examine the anisotropic characteristics of star formation regions in the central area of the Milky Way's bulge. 
Our model is based on the 2D dark energy effective field theory, and it utilises 2D data to derive parameters for a specific type of anisotropic distribution known as the 2D Lea-Nadarajah distribution. 
By applying this statistical method to a dataset of molecular clouds in the central zone, obtained from the ALMA observatory, we found that the model fits the data very well, with a correlation coefficient of 0.925. 
Our results indicate that the molecular clouds in this region are highly anisotropic in shape, and that the parameter values derived from our model can be used to constrain the parameters of the 2D distribution. 
These results have significant implications for our understanding of the dark sector of the universe, and they may provide a new framework for investigating the nature of dark energy and its effects on the expansion of the universe.

This paper introduces a novel approach to identifying Bell's Palsy by focusing on eye movement patterns in video footage.  Our eye-centered method involves analyzing eye movement metrics such as blink frequency, blink duration, and pupil dilation to detect signs of the condition.  As a result, we avoid the need for resource-intensive processing of entire video frames, which would require a more sophisticated model and increased computational capabilities.  Instead, we utilize a simple artificial neural network that processes short video clips centered on the eye region.  We validate our approach by testing it on a private dataset comprised of over 100 positive and 100 negative cases, demonstrating an average accuracy rate of 85% in detecting the condition.

Our analysis indicates that minute noise levels in qutrit-based quantum simulations of a scaled down version of quantum electrodynamics can have significant, noise-enhancement, 10-fold improvements in signal-to-noise ratio when compared to standard using qubit-based simulations.

In order to produce the most compact size for positron clouds, the optimal method of laser polarization on solid targets should be investigated. We simulated the interaction between intense lasers and metallic targets coated with dielectric layers using one-dimensional models. The choice of dielectric coating materials significantly impacts the yield of positrons. When a high-intensity, dielectric-coated nickel target was irradiated with an s-polarized laser, the positron cloud reached its minimum half-radius at 140 nm, compared to 260 nm with an p-polarized target.

A subgroup of a group G is considered wide if it intersects every conjugial subset of G. The subgroup width of G is the minimum intersection required for all subgroups of G. We investigate the relationship between subgroup intersections and specific properties of a group, particularly in relation to its composition factors. Our research reveals that if a group has finite subgroup width, a significant portion of its structure is permutable, and if it is solvable, its subgroup width is closely related to its derangement index. Conversely, if a group has an infinite subgroup width, there are specific indices where wide subgroups do not cover a substantial portion of the group.

This work introduces an innovative voltage-based temperature sensing technique suitable for low-power integrated circuits.  It is designed to meet the requirements for precise thermal management without significantly increasing power consumption.  As modern devices strive for better temperature control and comfort, especially in the context of sustainable development, this technique could contribute to efficient thermal management systems in low-power contexts.  For instance, when combined with a high-resolution Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC), this temperature sensing circuit can enable compact and comfortable devices with effective thermal control.  It is compatible with a wide range of supply voltages and operates seamlessly with standard 12-bit ADCs, making it versatile for a variety of applications.  It consumes a minimal amount of power - 14.5nW in a 65nm process - and can detect minute temperature changes of 0.24{\deg}C in 10us.  It features a compact design, occupying a compact 0.0195mm^2 area, and was verified through a series of tests.

The long-standing puzzle of why magnetic fields in some young stellar objects can remain strong for years despite rapid rotation and the associated magnetic instability is referred to as the magnetic decay paradox. A numerical study was conducted to discover the conditions under which axially symmetric magnetic fields can remain stable in three dimensions. The results show that magnetic fields can remain stable in stars with high rates of rotation, specifically when the magnetic field strength and the rotation speed both increase, and this condition is independent of the star's shape. To address the magnetic decay paradox, it is proposed that the axisymmetry of magnetic fields should be considered in stellar dynamics, as this could help preserve magnetic fields in rapidly rotating stars. Additionally, the axisymmetric magnetic fields may contribute to the generation of large-scale magnetic fields observed in stellar activity cycles.

The functional renormalization group (FRG) technique has been the primary approach for studying non-perturbative flow in quantum field theory. A recent development in this field has been linking the renormalization group's evolution to the flow of an effective action, which can be expressed as a function of field variables. This perspective paves the way for employing numerical renormalization group (NRG) methods in quantum field theory. In this paper, we propose a framework to evaluate flow-type renormalization group equations in the full functional space of quantum field theories, independent of approximations. A test case involving quantum field theories based on the effective stochastic differential equation (TSDE) model is presented. A new numerical algorithm is introduced to solve the flow-type FRG equations, which relies on the master equation method used for solving time-dependent Schrödinger's equation and effective TSGDE. The proposed method yields results that are in line with the existing approximate solutions of the loop expansion type for the beta function of the renormalized coupling constant in the QFT based on the TSGDE model. Additionally, a comparison is made with standard $O(N)$ model FRG results.

A music discovery and recommendation platform named "Pied Piper" has been developed in Panda's lab, built using the Meta Quest's immersive capabilities. By integrating cutting-edge technologies like panoramic vision, precise motion tracking, and immersive sound, Pied Piper music videos offer a unique and engaging experience that captivates fans and creates an intimate connection between artists and their audience. The platform is designed to facilitate live performances and create unforgettable moments, leveraging Meta Quest's technology to deliver an unparalleled experience.

This work introduces fundamental structures from differential geometry, including Riemannian geometry, torsion-free connections, and conformal geometry on Lie groupoids and stacks. The concepts rely on the associated bundles derived from the chosen Lie groupoid or stack. A key distinction from geometry on manifolds is that morphisms in such categories preserve these geometric structures only up to certain factors, representing the differential of a map or its conformal transformation. These 'up-to' properties are essential in the study of gauge theories, where geometric data is considered equivalent if related by such transformations. Specifically, two connections are regarded as equivalent if they share the same curvature under the differential map. Similarly, conformal geometries are defined as equivalent when their metrics are related by a positive scalar factor through the associated bundle.

Researchers have utilized 1.3 mm and 850 um observations to study 13 dense cores within the Dragon infrared dark cloud, discovering that 10 of these cores are expanding at a rate of 10^-5 radians per year. Notably, these inferring a dynamic core population within an LDCl, which may be on the cusp of forming massive stars. Furthermore, researchers have deduced that the observed expansion is not a result of tidal effects but rather an intrinsic property of the core. The expansion velocities within these cores are sufficient to influence the environment and potentially affect star formation processes.

Godel modal logics can be viewed as extensions of intutionistic propositional logic that incorporate relations describing accessibility between elements. Previous research has examined the algebraic and relational frameworks for various Godel modal logics, specifically those based on finite or denumerable sets of truth values. In this study, I explore algebraic and relational frameworks for a broader range of Godel modal logics, including some defined over uncountable sets of truth values. Additionally, I introduce the concept of a predicate T-bimodel and investigate its applicability to Godel modal logics.

LiDAR point clouds offer valuable, high-precision data for extracting key information and understanding spatial environments. Point cloud processing is applied in various settings, such as real estate surveying, urban planning, and environmental monitoring. Despite its effectiveness, traditional point cloud processing often falls short in delivering a comprehensive analysis of our surroundings. By integrating LiDAR point cloud data with other sources of information and advanced techniques for image and shape processing, we can enhance our ability to interpret our environment. This integration leads to the development of intelligent systems capable of perceiving and processing LiDAR point clouds in a manner similar to human intelligence.

Reciprocal random evolution on a sphere is analyzed, focusing on positive-definite functions that start at zero when two points coincide and become independent after coin tossing between them. A key property of such processes is their Markovian behavior at critical values, representing the distance between points. Coin tossing at continuous time rates, leads to discrete Markov chains. If these steps occur infinitely often and sum to a finite value, the limiting distances satisfy a specific renewal equation. The existence of positive-definite Markovian stagnant random fields is established, along with a class of fields where marked points interact and track their positions as Markovian particles. These solutions include functions that correspond to coalescing Brownian motions. Additionally, an infinite family of functions that represent record values of Brownian motion at exponential times, arises.

Using the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the Auger Observatory, researchers analyzed the directional correlation between the energies of neutrinos observed from 2016-2018 and the cosmic rays with extraordinary energies detected by the Auger Observatory in 2014-2018. The study found no significant spatial clusters in the direction data for neutrinos or cosmic rays, although a slight cluster with a statistical significance of 2.2 sigma was detected for cosmic rays in a specific energy range. When comparing the presence of cosmic rays near the path of neutrinos to what would be expected based on the cosmic rays' distribution alone, one instance was discovered with 3.7 sigma significance in the same specific energy range. These findings do not contradict the standard lambda cold dark matter model but highlight the importance of continuing the analysis with more data in the future.

The flow of liquid foams is heavily influenced by their internal texture, and this connection is even more apparent in thick foams. In these dense foams, the behavior is a blend of viscous and elastic characteristics. This research quantifies the friction within thick foams, and finds a direct correlation between a foam's friction and its yield stress. Notably, this internal friction is tied to the foam's contact area ratio, and displays distinct patterns during the foam's coarsening process. These findings can be applied to understand the viscosity of thick foams in a way that takes into account their yield stress.

This paper introduces a novel, comprehensive dataset containing 11,000 images across six skin cancer categories, known as HDFS. The dataset's images were annotated by dermatologists and a expert in melanoma detection, covering classes such as healthy skin, benign moles, dermatofibroma, and two types of cancer, seborrheic keratosis and melanoma. To test the dataset's performance, the proposed method SkinEn employs U-net architecture combined with an entropy-based outlier detection technique called Local Outlier Factor. By training two models - one for each class - and comparing anomaly scores, SkinEn effectively distinguishes skin cancer types, with an impressive 99.5% accuracy in identifying melanoma.

The steady-state behavior of the Newtonian fluid in a rotating Hele-Shaw cell, subject to centrifugal force, has been analyzed under the influence of a growing finger. By employing Darcy's law and utilizing phase-field simulation, researchers have gained valuable insights into how certain dimensionless parameters influence the finger's flexibility and fingering pattern formation. Specifically, the balance between the elastic forces and the capillary forces is identified as a key determinant in shaping the finger's morphology. The study reveals that elevated values of the elasticity parameter result in more complex patterns, whereas increased curvature of the finger's tip lead to patterns characterized by higher periodicity. Furthermore, the study finds that the elasticity parameter alone is insufficient to account for the fingering patterns observed, necessitating consideration of an additional parameter that reflects the magnitude of the elastic forces in relation to the capillary forces. Ultimately, the study establishes an inverse relationship between this parameter and the number of patterns observed, providing a means to classify the patterns into distinct categories.

We introduce a novel approach for calculating the linearized entropy production rate in time-dependent Hamiltonian systems through linearization of their evolution equations. Our method addresses the constraints of previous methods, which could not be applied to time-dependent systems and required perturbations around equilibrium states. By deriving the linearized entropy production from the time derivative of the phase space volume element, our approach eliminates these limitations and is illustrated with calculations of entropy production in the free expansion of a many-particle system, both with and without interparticle collisions.

A cycle-aromatic cluster in the cyclopentadiene molecule, C5H4, has been identified in two isomeric forms, ethynyl cyclopentadiene, using the SubMillimeter Array and ATOMBASE/ALMA observations. The cycle is found attached to a triple bond in the C2 position of the molecule. The study also confirms the presence of C5H4 in the benzene molecule, C6H4, and C5H4-C3H in a low-abundance molecular cloud, TMC-1. The cycles are present in extremely low concentrations, with the ethynyl cyclopentadiene isomers accounting for approximately 2 x 10^-9 and 6 x 10^-10 relative to ethynyl cyclopentadiene, respectively. Furthermore, the cycle-to-CCH ratio is calculated to be around 3 x 10^-5 and 1 x 10^-5, with the cycle-to-CN ratio being 1.5 x 10^-4 and 5 x 10^-5. These cycle abundances are comparable to those of other cyclic molecules, with the cycle-to-cyclopropyl ratio being 0.5 to 1.7. The cycle and cyclopropyl molecules may be formed through similar mechanisms, with the cycle-to-cyclopropyl abundance ratio being 0.9 when taking into account the difference in their

In neural machine translation, current models that use cross-entropy as a generation guide are limited because they only consider past decisions, which is a form of focus known as retroactive. ToLAF, proposed in this paper, expands on this by incorporating an attention mechanism that allows the model to prioritize specific target words before generating them, drawing on a principle called look-ahead focus. By replacing the source context computation with a dedicated focus mechanism, models using ToLAF can effectively utilize more relevant information, potentially improving translation quality. We further demonstrate that ToLAF can be applied to enhance existing generation methods, such as self-augmentation and list attention, by integrating the focus mechanism. All these improvements are easily incorporated into the standard attention framework with minimal additional training. We made the ToLAF framework available on the Opentran platform for further research and development.

Computer systems have evolved from mainframes to personal computers, and this advancement has been fueled by a shift in design philosophy.  A similar design shift is now needed in the computer grid.  Historically, the grid grew organically, and was formalized by adding a layer of management on top of it.  A more innovative approach is now required - one that integrates the essential grid features into each computer system, and accelerates their development through co-evolution.  By making grid functionality a built-in aspect of every computer system, we can translate the grid into a language that is native to each machine's operating system and design philosophy.  This approach is exemplified by Apple's seamless integration of design and functionality in their computer systems.  And, it is being applied in projects like AppleTV+, which leverages a built-in grid functionality to stream high-quality video content.  By making grid functionality a built-in aspect of every computer system, we can unlock new levels of performance and efficiency, and pave the way for a more intuitive and seamless user experience.

In a unified dark matter-dark energy framework, we investigate how dark matter's dissipation influences the universe's evolution. By applying a holographic dark matter model with the dark matter-holographic relationship, we determine the equation of state for UNDM. Our calculations reveal that UNDM's equation of state is affected by its dissipation rate and universe size, with the rate of dissipation having the capacity to prevent the big rip scenario. UNDM emerges as a viable candidate for dark energy, with its properties being shaped by its dissipation process and holographic characteristics.

Understanding the complex nature of curiosity in learners within a group learning context remains an under-explored area in educational research. Curiosity, a key driver of motivation and a crucial skill for preparing young people for a rapidly changing world, is difficult to measure due to its subjective and individualized perception. To address this challenge, our proposed method utilizes a combination of non-invasive techniques, including eye tracking and self-reported interest levels, to track the curiosity levels of young people learning a new language in a group setting. By analyzing both verbal and non-verbal cues, our study aims to provide a more holistic understanding of curiosity in a group learning environment. The results of our pilot research indicate that eye tracking can effectively capture unexpressed curiosity in learners, while self-reported interest levels serve as a reliable indicator of expressed curiosity. Furthermore, our findings suggest that curiosity is a multifaceted phenomenon that is best measured through a combination of both techniques. The implications of our proposed method are far-reaching, suggesting that it has the potential to inform the design of more effective and personalized learning experiences.

Moving beyond a Gaussian covariance framework, we've expanded a specific type of dependence structure, Mat\'ern Gaussian models, to a broader range under the condition of a given graph. This new approach allows for the examination of both traditional Gaussian covariance and more intricate, graph-based relationships, potentially offering improved robustness to outliers and extreme events in a controlled manner. By leveraging positive definite square roots of certain matrices, we demonstrate that generalizing these models maintains the benefits of a precision approach while accommodating a variety of covariance structures - including Mat\'ern covariances for stationary data and pre-defined distance-based models like Mat\'ern for non-stationary data. We've also developed an efficient simulation technique based on the Cholesky factorization of an edge-based matrix, which shows comparable accuracy and performance to direct sampling using the Cholesky factor of the full positive definite matrix.

Urban road networks are complex and highly interconnected systems that can be effectively monitored using a large number of ridesourcing vehicles in real-time. Supervisory control schemes for road networks are critical in maintaining optimal traffic conditions, with potential actions including directing vehicles to alternative routes, regulating access to the network from external roads, and controlling the flow of vehicles into the network from external roads. A new approach to achieving optimal performance has been proposed, which uses a detection and control framework based on state estimation through a statistical method known as Kalman filtering. This approach enables real-time identification of the actual road network performance, estimation of its unobserved states, and implementation of actions to maintain optimal conditions. The proposed detection and control framework was tested using a large-scale dataset from Los Angeles, California, with around 130,000 roads and 3 million trips made by 850,000 ridesourcing vehicles during peak hours in 2019. The results showed that the framework can meet real-time processing requirements, successfully identified the actual performance of the road network, and achieved optimal detection of 99.99% of roads within one hour. The framework's capability to track minor deviations from optimal performance was also demonstrated, with 99.9988% of roads within 5 minutes of optimal detection.

Neutrino and dark matter interactions that remain invisible can be described using effective field theories, and any such new physics can influence certain decay processes like the $J/\psi$ decay into a gamma ray and something undetectable. By utilizing a newly discovered anomaly in this process, researchers have been able to place a limit on the effective operators in these theories, assuming a neutrino-dark matter mass difference of under 5.4 GeV, resulting in a operator coefficient of less than $4.5 \times 10^{-5}$ GeV$^{-6}$ at a 95% confidence level. This finding is depicted in a plot, and a detailed explanation of the calculation is outlined in a separate document.
Previous research has already established modified standard dissimilar stepsize implicit semi-implicit methods on non-standard equations, already adjusting for the equation's 'non-standard' nature.

Multivariate functional time series analysis has gained significant attention in recent years due to the ability to handle complex, high-dimensional data sets. This paper introduces multivariate functional singular spectrum analysis, a method capable of handling different dimensional domains for both variables and time. We examine its asymptotic behavior and conduct an analogous study for methods using a fixed number of variables. Additionally, this research is among the first to explore spectral density estimation with a continuous variable framework in multiple dimensions.

Recent studies suggest that self-supervised edge detection methods may struggle with certain types of attacks due to their tendency to produce excessively certain judgments incorrectively. This paper addresses a critical issue: the concept of "both both" performance in classification systems, which measures both classification accuracy and confidence levels. We argue that most current research concentrates on one aspect of "both both" performance, neglecting the balance between correctness and confidence. Moreover, we observe that existing anti-spoofing technologies are particularly susceptible to a novel class of attacks we name "super spoofing". Through detailed theoretical analysis and extensive practical validation, we demonstrate that edge detection systems, in their quest to minimize error rates, often become overstable and overreactive, excessively certain in their incorrect judgments. This phenomenon arises from the characteristic of minimax optimization used in these systems. Additionally, we find that minimizing uncertainty can be an effective defense against super spoofing attacks by limiting the range of uncertainty levels. This paper is, to our knowledge, among the first to thoroughly investigate and clarify the underlying mechanisms of edge detection systems in the context of "both both" performance, and it also reveals a common vulnerability across various classification systems named "super spoofing".

The overall persistence of one-dimensional random walks is typically studied through various persistent probabilities. These probabilities are categorized into two types: global persistence, defined as the time the random walk spends being positive relative to the total duration, and local persistence, defined by the time spent at zero given a specific starting time when the walk is about to change sign. Previous research has established the asymptotic behavior of various persistence types when one-dimensional random walks are observed over an extensive period. In contrast, this study focuses on the relationship between local and global persistence properties, specifically examining the probability distribution of local persistence given that the random walk has a certain persistent duration. This study differs from earlier studies in two key aspects: it investigates persistence on a scale comparable to the characteristic length of random walks and has an innovative setting for modeling the relationship between local and global persistence. The research findings demonstrate the possibility of the local persistence distribution converging to a specific type of gamma distribution under certain conditions, as well as the asymptotic behavior of persistence for random walks with a significantly shorter observation period. The results of this study are intended to have broader relevance to the understanding of random walk dynamics and may have broader implications for related fields.

Plasma sources are crucial components in plasma devices, and understanding their plasma characteristics is essential for successful experiments.  However, limited data on some plasma sources hinders meaningful comparisons and experiment planning.  As a step toward improving this situation, a comprehensive measurement of plasma parameters was performed for the IShTAR source, a compact helicon plasma source.  Previous studies on this source were mostly in CCR mode, but it was demonstrated that switching to helical plasma mode (hel mode) significantly enhances plasma density.  In this research, both modes were compared, and in hel mode, a plasma density of 3.5x10^11 m^-3, plasma temperature of 0.35 eV, and biased voltage of -170 V were achieved.  A detailed analysis of the discharge components in both modes was done, and a comprehensive set of plasma parameters was provided for future reference and planning of experiments with the ISource.

In comparison to conventional chemical pesticides, microbial pesticides possess several advantages, which can be modelled using a system that incorporates a bacterium's ability to prey on insects and release toxins. This system's effectiveness relies on modifying parameters, and a proposed model can account for this by incorporating a parameter to reflect the bacterium's predation and toxin-release mechanisms in a more realistic manner. Analysis of the model's stability and long-term behavior indicates that certain conditions are necessary for achieving desired outcomes, and numerical simulations demonstrate that certain conditions lead to a stable population of insects, while others result in an oscillating pattern. Furthermore, an optimal strategy is identified for inferring the best course of action to achieve a desired result.

A histopathology image analysis is often time-consuming and expensive for pathologists to perform on a per-nucleus basis, prompting researchers to shift their focus to region-based classification tasks. However, the high density of nuclei within tissue sections poses challenges for segmenting individual cells, and as a result, researchers are instead exploring methods for shifting class labels from the tissue to the nucleus level. This paper presents a histopathology dataset called PolyPro, which is unique in its multi-class, multi-label annotations and shifts class labels from the tissue to the nucleus level. Additionally, we propose a method for converting the task from nucleus identification to nucleus segmentation, which we term Nucleus Segmentation Network, and demonstrate its efficacy on our dataset.

In the context of the local exchange theorem, we investigate odd special orthogonal and symplectic groups, denoted as $S\Omega(d,q)$ and $Sp(d,q)$, where $q$ is a prime power that is not equal to $2$, and classify their local extensions, with 'locality' defined by adjacency in a graph representing the Cayley graph of $S\Omega(d,q)$ and $Sp(d,q)$.

Zhang and Li previously provided a definition for graphs G that have a hamiltonian path in their repeated line graphs $\Lambda_2(G)$, and established characterizations under certain conditions. However, they had not given a definition or partial characterizations for graphs G that have a hamiltonian path in $\Lambda_2(G)$ in the more general case. In this paper, we provide a definition for graphs G that are pre-2line hamiltonian path, and we obtain both a new character of graphs that are pre-2line hamiltonian path and also a character of pre-2line hamiltonian path graphs in a specific case. In addition, we examine the relationship between hamiltonian path index and vertex transitive graphs.

Cell death due to pyroptosis, an inflammatory process, can lead to the spread of inflammation in the lungs during SARS-CoV-2 infection. A single-cell mathematical model was developed to analyze pyroptosis, using it to represent the rapid inflammation-induced cell death that occurs during the infection. A phase portrait of the system's dynamics and specific parameters, particularly those affected by anti-inflammatory medication like dexamethasone, are explored in this single-cell mathematical model.

External factors that affect an agent's learning process, such as irrelevant state variables and state-based rewards, can significantly hinder the learning process. In a reinforcement learning scenario, an agent's primary goal is to maximize the rewards it receives by making optimal decisions. However, if there are additional, unconnected state variables or rewards that are unrelated to the agent's actions, the agent's ability to learn the true cause-and-effect relationship between its actions and the resulting rewards gets complicated. Recent research has shown that in order for an agent to efficiently maximize the rewards, it must be able to distinguish between these exogenous components and those that are internally linked. In order to make this distinction clearer, we propose a method that makes it easier for an agent to do so, thus simplifying the agent's task. In order to test the effectiveness of this method, we designed a task that requires agents to distinguish between causally connected states and exogenous components. In order to test the agents' ability to do so, we used retargeting, a method that transfers the same rewards to an altered environment. In order to transfer the rewards, we used a state that is minimally interfering with the exogenous components. In our experiments, we used a variety of agents and environments to test the effectiveness of this method. In order to make it easier for the agents to do so, we used a method that transferred the same rewards to an altered environment. In our results, this method made it easier for the agents to

The blockchain industry demands high reliability for smart contracts, with a particular focus on data correctness and the prevention of reentrancy attacks. Although platforms like Ethereum offer substantial transaction volumes and profitability incentives, these benefits come with significant risks. Traditional programming languages are proven capable of delivering the necessary reliability for blockchain applications, but they fall short in handling cryptocurrency payments and platform-specific state machines. This paper introduces a new set of refinement types for the Tezos programming language, augmenting them with module system extensions and module imports to facilitate module composition. Additionally, it presents a module-based validator for Tezos smart contracts that leverages refinement types to ensure correctness and reliability.

Due to their effectiveness in analyzing complex systems, graph-based machine learning methods have gained significant attention. Among these advances, Graph Convolutional Neural Networks (GCNNs) have proven particularly useful for their ability to incorporate nonlinear functions and adaptive parameters into traditional matched filtering concepts. This study supports a matched filtering interpretation of GCNNs, reinforcing the notion that they refine the filtering process on graph structures. Furthermore, it proposes an enhanced filtering method based on positive factorization of graph structures, which supports training using cross-entropy loss and provides insights into the GCNN's operation. The proposed approach also allows for elements of graph theory to be utilized in designing and improving GCNNs for specific tasks, and demonstrates this by applying the matched filtering concept to address issues of model overfitting in graph-based machine learning methods.

Einstein's general relativity can be re-expressed through the language of Chern-Simons gauge theory using the Ashtekar variables, the complexified connection of the SU(2) group. This reformulation has been extended to include a scalar field that transforms as a triplet under the SU(2) group, utilizing the Bardeen-Tyonen-Coleman-S Jackiw (BTCC) action. By incorporating the Bardeen-Myers (BM) boundary terms, we successfully eliminate unwanted degrees of freedom at the boundary. In the near-extremal limit of the Einstein-scalar gauge theory (ESG) graviton hair black hole, we observe a near-flat spacetime horizon with constant, complexified SU(2) connection values. This allows us to map the near-extremal ESG black hole solutions onto their BTCC+BM counterpart, demonstrating the equivalence of their action values and the consistency of their Hamiltonian values at zero. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between the BMS mass and the Einstein mass, and show that the BMS angular momentum of the ESG rotating black hole is composed of both classical and quantum contributions from the SU(2) connection values, with the latter being non-zero. Additionally, we prove that the Bardeen-Myers term contributes to the BMS mass of the ESG graviton hair soliton solution, with the total BMS mass being zero.

We've discovered an intriguing correlation between the number of branes in a specific type of theory and a property known as gluino number reversal. This theory, referred to as duality, mirrors the relationship between objects and their anti-objects, but only applies to systems with an equal number of branes and anti-branes. Through specific transformations, we're able to mirror the relationship, reducting the systems to gluino number reversal. This enables the equivalence of two systems that differ solely in the sign of their anomaly.

One prevalent technique in strain-based ultrasound elastography is image quality improvement through strain interpolation, but this technique has the drawback of introducing lateral shifts that complicate strain calculation. While some methods exist to correct these shifts, the conventional 2x2 strain interpolation approach still leaves a certain margin of error. This study presents an innovative strain interpolation method called the virtual source synthetic aperture (VSSA) approach, which accurately estimates lateral shifts and yields more precise strain calculations. The VSSA method applies a synthetic aperture approach to the shifted data, allowing the beamforming process to accurately locate the target source and reduce the estimated lateral shifts. Experimental results indicate that the VSSA approach yields more accurate shift estimations and reliable elastographic images, even at high beam angles. Furthermore, the VSSA strain interpolation method requires a minimal computational overhead, making it a straightforward and effective means of correcting lateral shifts in ultrasound strain-based elastography.

In recent years, research has shown the effectiveness of combining logic and proof techniques with algorithmic concepts, suggesting a potential framework for next-generation programming languages. This idea is further explored by Cecka and Pucella, who propose an innovative approach called "logical pseudocode." This novel framework is designed to integrate algorithmic and proof techniques, allowing for the creation of more robust and verified programming solutions. 

Our work extends this proposal by demonstrating the feasibility of "logical pseudocode" through the development of logical versions of fundamental algorithmic techniques, including iteration, recursion, and co-recursion. These advancements are supported by the establishment of specific proof principles, such as invariants, well-founded relations, and co-variants, which ensure the correctness and reliability of the resulting code. 

The efficacy of "logical pseudocode" is highlighted through the presentation of enhanced proofs for the correctness of classic algorithms, such as co-Hoare triple-based iteration trivias, iteration-transpilation and distributed consensus, and a co-recursive proof of the correctness of the stream-merging algorithm. The results of this research are made available for download in the form of a full implementation on the NGL platform.

The concept of Boolean Ramsey theory, a branch of combinatorics, focuses on identifying subsets within $2^n$ that possess $V$-poset properties as $n$ increases, with a particular interest in one-dimensional convex chains. This line of research has yielded numerous positive results, but also exposed limitations in $V$-poset form factor rates, often leaving room for improvement. This paper aims to enhance this understanding by presenting an improved variant of one such hypothesis, specifically targeting a scenario where an infinite set within $2^n$ adheres to a one-dimensional convex chain structure with a specified form factor. This paper presents both a refined upper limit of $n/4$ as well as a corresponding $n/5$ lower limit for this scenario.

In the context of dynamic data streams, we investigate the $k$-cluster problem in high-dimensional spaces by introducing a novel algorithm that leverages an existing approximation scheme. This algorithm leverages an existing $O(\sqrt{d})$-approximation dynamic $k$-cluster algorithm and a specific reduction technique to produce $O(k^\epsilon O(\sqrt{d}))$-approximate optimal solutions. We can refine this result to incorporate time factors, resulting in nearly optimal dynamic $k$-cluster centers solutions across various time frames for data dimensions $d$.

Multi-agent learning frameworks have been successfully applied to train
real-world robots for tasks requiring navigation and task completion in
complex environments. However, these settings often involve large state
spaces that can slow down convergence and lead to suboptimal policy
development. To tackle this problem, we propose a novel approach called
Hierarchical Decompositions (HD) for enhancing the efficiency of the
stochastic chase-and-evasion game. This approach divides the game into
smaller, more manageable parts, allowing the agents to learn policies at
different levels of abstraction. We demonstrate the effectiveness of HD
by applying it to a real-life scenario where a service robot must navigate
and avoid collisions with an uncooperative exploration robot in a multi-room
environment. Experimental results show significant improvements in convergence
speed and accuracy when using HD compared to standard methods.

We explore the concept of nontransitive likelihoods using rock-paper-scissors as an example, where there's a cyclic likelihood among players. A corresponding nontransitive likelihood can be extracted from a given transitive set by randomly selecting people and comparing their incomes. Furthermore, we've found that cyclic likelihoods can be found easily in real-world data sets such as rock-paper-scissors data and lizard speed data. However, when we consider people's actual speeds and ages, a nontransitive set emerges less frequently.

Recently, deep learning techniques have been successful in restoring low-dose CT images, which is particularly useful in clinical settings due to the reduced radiation exposure. However, there are variations in the image quality of low-dose CT images even from the same dose, making a single restoration model inadequate. In this paper, we propose AdaIN-Switchable CycleGAN, a novel approach using the cycle-consistency framework and adaptive instance normalization to restore low-dose CT images with limited low-dose training data. Experimental results on several clinical datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method, which outperforms several state-of-the-art methods.

Recently, dialog understanding systems have achieved great success with the use of multi-task classification and multi-task learning techniques. However, both techniques come with significant costs, necessitating a large amount of labeled data and incurring complex models that are hard to optimize. In this paper, we introduce a novel approach called SPACE-2, a tree-structured semi-supervised contrastive pre-training framework for dialog understanding tasks. The framework combines three key components: (1) semi-supervised contrastive pre-training for learning high-quality initial representations of dialogs, (2) node-level multi-task classification, and (3) sequence-level multi-task classification. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we conducted a series of experiments on the MultiWOZ 2.0 dataset, a widely used benchmark for multi-domain dialog understanding tasks. The results show that our method outperforms the state-of-the-art techniques, achieving substantial improvements in sequence-level tasks and satisfactory performance in node-level tasks. Notably, our approach requires a significantly smaller amount of labeled data, coming with a reduction of 99.9% compared to full labeling.

This research paper proves that a certain type of manifold, which represents an ideal fluid spacetime, is conformally equivalent to a statistical sphere when a conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton is involved. It also demonstrates that the potential function of the soliton is either the scalar function or its conformal factor is a p-laplacian of the scalar function, thereby indicating the conformal equivalence of the manifold to a statistical sphere. Furthermore, it is proven that the manifold is conformally equivalent to a statistical sphere when the mean curvature of the conformal metric is the p-Laplacian of the Laplacian of the Ricci curvature. This condition is satisfied when the Laplacian of the Ricci curvature equals the p-Laplacian of a constant, thus confirming the conformal equivalence of the ideal fluid spacetime with a conformal Ricci-Yamabe soliton to a statistical sphere.

By applying the total angular momentum and energy constraints within the random phase approximation, we investigated the rotational characteristics of spinning, distorted neutron halos with an intermediate density distribution. Notably, rotating distorted nuclei exhibited two distinct frequency modes of oscillation in their density distribution, each with its own rotational inertia and energy spectrum. Our analysis of a rotating $^{11}$Li revealed significant decoupling in rotational behavior between the neutron halo and the core.

We've significantly upgraded the BasicVSR network for video super-resolution, specifically addressing the issues of signal deterioration and misalignment that happen during the processing of video frames. To mitigate these problems, we employed gapped convolution to prevent the loss of information and cross-scale alignment to improve the structural coherence. Furthermore, we introduced a series of complementary video enhancement techniques. When combined, our improved network achieved superior video super-resolution results compared to the original BasicVSR on multiple benchmarks, requiring very little additional computation.

Precision studies and searches for new physics at a 3 TeV muon collider can leverage the clean environment provided by initial state radiated photons and an associated vector boson, such as a $W$ boson. Despite the photon radiation being difficult to detect fully, the associated lepton from the $W$ decay allows experiments to efficiently select this event type. This letter presents initial research establishing the feasibility of utilizing processes where the cross section is dominated by the photon-W-boson approximation. Further work is necessary to refine boundaries within the valid region and explore processes with subleading contributions.

In multi-task reinforcement learning, using a single policy for multiple tasks can lead to the model catastrophically interfering with other tasks. In this paper, we propose an innovative solution to this problem by introducing modular networks that avert this interference. We integrate a switching network with a set of task-specific sub-networks, which together form a structured architecture to learn both the single policy and a set of switching signals. This design isolates sub-networks from one another, limiting their interactions to only with the switching network. As an outcome, we observe that modular networks consistently outperform their non-switching network counterparts in model-based multi-task reinforcement learning. Notably, we also discover that certain switching modules naturally develop into a hierarchical structure, which can be used to decompose complex reward functions into simpler components. We empirically validate these findings in multi-task reinforcement learning, first on a grid-world navigation task and then on a complex multi-task robotic manipulation task.

This paper provides new upper bound formulas for solution changes with respect to distance and time for various types of nonlinear equations, including the porous medium type equations and the fast diffusion type equations, on a specific kind of complete, non-compact metric measure space with a compact boundary. The equations evolve over time and are influenced by the geometry of the underlying space. The obtained estimates are in the form of Gronwall-Lagrange type inequalities. As a result, similar upper bound formulas can be derived for the solutions. Furthermore, some previous results in this field can be inferred from the theorems presented in this paper. Additionally, concrete examples demonstrate the application of the established inequalities.

We delve into the foundational aspects of mathematics, focusing on Godel's incompleteness theorems, which are considered primary limitations of classical first-order logic. Notably, Godel's second incompleteness theorem establishes that the consistency of basic mathematics cannot be proven by the mathematics itself. A crucial component of this theorem is the ability to translate mathematical statements back and forth within the same logical system. However, this translation technique can be utilized to demonstrate that if certain statements are true, then the logical system can also prove its own consistency. Using this approach, Godel was able to create an alternative statement with equivalent meaning to the original, thereby proving that the system is either incomplete or susceptible to alternative interpretations. This same reasoning can be employed to make similar assertions about other complex propositions, such as those related to set theory.

In this study, we establish a local three-balls inequality for monogenic functions within the context of Clifford analysis. As a direct consequence, we derive an local three-cubes inequality for eigenfunctions of the Dirac operator, thereby extending earlier results from complex variable theory and real harmonic function analysis. These findings enable us to obtain corresponding local Caccioppoli's inequality and local mean value inequality for monogenic functions as well as entire monogenic polynomials.

In the most recent year of available data, nearly 90% of the world's people lacked access to safe drinking water, clean sanitation, and reliable nutrition. This research presents a fair and efficient method for sequentially making choices from a high-dimensional space, taking into account a given set of weights for each point. Our algorithm guarantees that the final set of chosen points will be within a specific range of equity, and can be efficiently implemented for certain-dimensional spaces.

Robotic systems that use eye-to-hand cameras are essential for performing real-time image analysis and manipulating objects.  However, the precise alignment of these cameras is often affected by slight inaccuracies in calibration due to the nature of the used semi-flexible lenses.  As a result, obtaining an accurate camera internal parameter set becomes a significant challenge.  Current methods of calibration are usually costly and require the assistance of human operators to manually adjust the lens or employ expensive external equipment to measure the flexible lens parameters.  In this research, a novel approach to calibration is proposed that relies on a unique eye-to-hand dataset, in which a human operator places an object within view of the camera and adjusts the camera's position and orientation to achieve a certain visual effect.  The distinctive characteristics of this data allow a machine learning model to be trained to predict the accurate camera internal parameters from a single, unlabelled image.  This model is then capable of calibrating a variety of eye-to-hand cameras with semi-flexible lenses, regardless of the specific camera model or camera sensor used.  Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach by showing improved object segmentation and object pose estimation performance when using the eye-to-hand dataset that has been adjusted with the internal parameters set by the machine learning model.

The Gaussian Markov Monte Carlo (GMMC) method is an advanced technique used in subsurface flow modeling and flow-based geophysical inversion to create realizations that adhere to prior conditions. This study presents a novel application of the Conditional GAN (CGAN) model for estimating the posterior distribution in inverse problems. By formulating the CGAN as a regularized objective function, we can leverage the strength of the Mean Squared Error in approximating the posterior. In addition to the CGMC, our approach leverages the power of the CGAN to estimate the complex components of the posterior distribution. Leveraging the strengths of both the CGAN and the CGMC results in a more efficient and accurate estimation of the posterior distribution.

This article examines the possibility of invariant solutions in dynamic systems described by a fractional order, using a specific example where previous research has shown that certain invariant solutions do not exist when the order is less than two. We provide a general method for solving the time transformation associated with a given differential equation, and demonstrate its application to a specific system to obtain an solution that is valid for all values of the order q. Additionally, we explore the stability of this invariant solution using a novel approach, and investigate how the parameter q affects the stability of this system.

Next-generation wireless networks, utilizing Terahertz frequencies, are being explored to overcome 5G capacity limitations, by utilizing short-distance, direct links. However, due to rapid signal degradation at THz frequencies, beyond a few meters, more flexible and longer-distance communication is required. Sub-wavelength beam training is being proposed to allow choosing multiple beams per antenna sector, but results in an enormous search space that hampers efficient packet-based beam training algorithms. This paper investigates reinforcement learning applications for selecting optimal beams in direct, single-hop THz links, demonstrating its potential to learn effective beam selection patterns with minimal or no data. The paper also evaluates the algorithm's performance in non-line-of-sight environments, by utilizing intermediate devices to create multi-hop paths.

Our analysis of 11 recent observations of the pulsar B1133+16, conducted between 2010 and 2021, involved measuring scintillation patterns to understand how the interstellar medium affects radio signals. By analyzing these patterns, specifically the temporal and spectral scintillation rates and the scintillation bandwidth, we were able to calculate the size and location of electron clouds in the space between Earth and the pulsar. Notably, the electron clouds in 2010 and 2021 were found in different regions, indicating a shift from an outer electron cloud in the middle of the pulsar's path to electron clouds at both the beginning and end of its path. In contrast, in 2012, 2014, 2014a, 2014b, 2020, and 2021, only inner electron clouds were detected. These findings suggest that the electron clouds are dynamic and change over time, offering valuable insights into the behavior of the interstellar medium.

This paper presents a novel generative model named Quasi-Periodic WaveNet (QPNet) to enhance the limited pitch control of the original WaveNet (NWNet) and MultiPeriodic WaveNet (MPNet) in speech synthesis. Unlike previous autoregressive generative models that utilize Expanded Convolution Neural Networks (ENet) for quicker inference speed, NPNet is built on a non-maximally pooled convolution neural network. The key difference lies in NPNet's application of an additional assumption: the use of signal quasi-periodicity allows it to discard the pitch-dependent expansion of the analysis filter, which is central to NWNet and ENet. NPNet is capable of directly modeling periodic speech waveforms, excluding noise, leading to an inefficient allocation of parameters in NPNet when applied to synthesize speech. The NPNet model is then optimized by incorporating a residual connection that accounts for the noise component of speech synthesis, which is not ignored as assumed by the quasi-periodicity of the signal. The network design of NPNet is further justified by a quasi-periodicity-based decomposition of the conditional probability of speech waveforms. The efficacy of the proposed model is confirmed by numerical experiments demonstrating its superior performance compared to both NWNet and MPNet in pitch control during speech synthesis.

This study introduces MADARi, a comprehensive annotation and spelling correction tool for under-resourced Semitic languages, specifically focusing on Classical and Modern Arabic. Additionally, the research team has employed this platform to annotate a dataset of 10,000 morphemes in Modern Standard Arabic, and it has been integrated with state-of-the-art tools for morphological segmentation and lexical lookup to streamline the annotation process.

This paper photochemically models temperate terrestrial planets, considering both atmospheric composition and stellar type. It characterizes spectral properties of these worlds through a combination of transmission and emission spectroscopy. It demonstrates how atmospheric gases such as water, carbon dioxide, methane, and ozone can be identified in the 0.3 to 2.0 micrometer wavelength range. It also highlights the significance of ultraviolet-induced surface heating and ozone absorption in shaping the spectral features of water. It further explores the impact of high-altitude hydrocarbon haze on the spectral characteristics of planets orbiting cooler K and M stars. It assesses the influence of stellar activity on observed emission spectra, emphasizing the difficulty in distinguishing active stellar spots from the planet's own emission. It calculates a temperate, Venus-like planet's equilibrium temperature and observed emission spectrum, which are significantly affected by UV-induced surface heating.

To differentiate between zero-energy peaks caused by Majorana and other mechanisms in a tunneling spectrum, we suggest a setup where a majorana peak can stand out from other peaks. We propose using a setup where the superconductor is connected to a classical ohmic resistor. By incorporating this resistance into the theory of tunneling, and comparing it to a case where the superconductor has no dissipation, or is connected to a BCS reservoir, we can see that a unique signature of a majorana peak is that it scales with the resistance. Additionally, the peak associated with a majorana mode is characterized by an exponential tail that originates from a linear tail in the tunneling conductance, which is a tell-tale sign of a majorana peak.

With an increasing number of vehicles and roads in developing nations, the risk of road accidents is rising. Research indicates that poorly maintained road surfaces significantly contribute to road accidents. The deterioration of road surfaces over time necessitates regular flaw detection and repair measures. However, the labor-intensive and costly nature of manual inspection processes has prompted the development of a more efficient, user-friendly, and data-driven inspection system. This paper introduces an innovative inspection system that employs a unified approach, integrating a centralized database, a web application, and a cutting-edge flaw detection technique based on color segmentation and support vector machines. The system's core is a purpose-built, multi-functional device that captures high-resolution road images and transmits them to a centralized server for processing and data management.

This paper introduces a bicategorical framework for shadows, demonstrating its equivalence to a reversed, uncurried 2-categorical form, and subsequently unbcurrying it to reveal marks of compact cloaks as generating sets for their surrounding environment.

Recently, noise-based data augmentation techniques have gained popularity in
deep learning due to their effectiveness in introducing controlled disturbances
into training images, thereby improving the generalization capabilities of
trained models. While various methods exist for generating visual noise, most
existing approaches either rely on pre-defined textures or employ interactive
tools that require user input. In this paper, I propose an unsupervised learning
framework for automatically identifying visual noise without user intervention.
This proposed method, which I call UNLN, employs an unsupervised learning
approach to minimize the step size of model updates in order to force a model
to confuse distinct object classes with visual noise. To evaluate the
efficacy of the proposed method, I conducted experiments using object
detection models on the MS COCO dataset, which demonstrated that textures
identified through UNLN can enhance the performance of hard-to-detect objects
when incorporated as noise in training images.

This research presents a novel type of graph neural network called Lorentzian Graph Neural Networks (LGNNs), which employ a Lorentzian activation function to mitigate the limitations of the ReLU activation function. The ReLU activation function, widely used in traditional graph neural networks like Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Transformer models, contributes positively to optimization but causes the hierarchical separation issue due to its lack of continuity. The LGNNs, in contrast, offer an alternative that maintains enhanced continuity while mitigating the hierarchical separation problem. Furthermore, LGNNs exhibit superior performance in certain tasks that require precise classification, such as node attribute prediction, outperforming ReLU-based models like R-GAT. Additionally, LGNNs demonstrate improved robustness against adversarial attacks, resulting in greater accuracy and stability.

The primary objective of this research is to pinpoint a hidden sound source within a specific frequency range, given measurements of the sound within a limited area. These measurements allow us to determine how the source interacts with a solid object through an acoustic connection. The problem becomes more intricate due to the coupled nature of the frequencies within the area and the solid object, as well as the fact that we don't have complete information about the shape of the object or the properties of the material it's made from. We develop a new approach to solve this challenging issue and demonstrate its effectiveness on a known object with a known sound source. The results show that our method can accurately identify the hidden source, but convergence is only achieved when we have a good initial estimate of the frequencies within the area. The success of this approach can be improved by using prior knowledge about the shape of the object and the material it's made from, as well as by regularizing the inverse problem of identifying the sound source. The results of these different strategies are demonstrated in this research.

In optics, compressing light into optical cavities is a common and well-documented phenomenon. A question arises whether the same applies to mechanics, specifically about the ability to compress mechanical resonators and whether this is achievable through optomechanical coupling. We investigate the option of generating a steady-state optomechanical state that is compressed in both optical and mechanical modes through the coupling of the two modes. By analyzing a system with two optomechanical modes connected in a loop, and considering various configurations of the system, including an increase in optical nonlinearity, we examine the feasibility of creating such a hybrid state. Our study reveals that while there are limitations, it is indeed possible to create an optomechanical state that exhibits compression in both modes.

This study presents an extension of the basic mu-calculus by incorporating a form of differentiation, resulting in a comprehensive logical framework capable of expressing both scalar and vectorial properties. The proposed framework, known as the mu-calculus with entities, can represent the rate of change of formulas in relation to an underlying mathematical object, and has a complete characterization via an algebraic structure that combines Hom-superdistributive lattices with a given vector space. Furthermore, every specification within the logic can decomposed into a sum of characteristic functions that reflect the essential properties of the set defined by that specification, and these functions can be obtained through a recursive analysis of the specification's structure. The characterisation of the Flat-Module provides a foundation for a complete mathematical interpretation of the logic that incorporates both duality and rate of differentiation.

We propose a novel exponential delay discounting model incorporating the
concept of 'effective temperature' and the Tsallis distribution. By applying
the Tsallis distribution, we show that delay discounting rates vary in response
to the amount of delay, the size of the reward, and the 'effective temperature',
all of which deviate from conventional behavior observed in experiments.
Furthermore, we introduce two alternative discounting frameworks based on
the Tsallis distribution: one where decisions are influenced by a maximum
or minimum expected utility, and another by a expected or extreme value, yielding
different discounting rate variations with respect to the parameters of
effective temperature, delay, and reward.

We demonstrate that the harmonic gauge in Hefty Gravity fully specifies the metric's four degrees of freedom, completely determining the difference between Hefft Gravity and General Relativity's harmonic coordinate expressions as a harmonic gauge-specific function. Furthermore, we show that another equivalent expression for this difference exists, valid across different harmonic gauge functions.

A signed graph is created by assigning signed edges to the edges of a regular graph. The concept of expanded double covers of signed graphs is new, and provides a foundation for studying expanded graphs and graph homomorphisms in relation to signed graphs. This new framework is useful in understanding parameters like the circular chromatic number and Tait's conjecture regarding expanded double covers and the circular chromatic number of graphs.

The study examines how nonperiodic canonical quantum systems, which are not confined to a finite space, correspond to classical statistical mechanics in a similar way. It demonstrates that the canonical quantum system's density matrix can be converted into a Weyl form, much like the classical classical density function. Both systems, classical and quantum, maintain a long-term stable state that is indicative of their equilibrium. Additionally, the study finds that the quantum classical equilibrium state corresponds to the classical classical state when observed through a Weyl-Wigner transformation.

We briefly discuss the concept of negative absolute temperature, which has gained interest due to recent experiments achieving such temperatures. Within the framework of statistical mechanics, we discuss the relationship between negative temperature, population inversion, and the limitations of the canonical ensemble, which considers only two energy levels. We suggest that, for a system with two accessible negative temperature levels, the ratio of particles in those levels is greater than one, and similarly for all higher energy levels. We also argue that in a system with negative temperature, the ratio of particles in adjacent levels is always greater than one, which implies that the ratio of particles in any two levels is also greater than one. Finally, we propose that a system with negative temperature can still exhibit coherent behavior, such as that seen in the microwave generation of a laser, and that the issue with the ratio of particles in a two-level system can be resolved by considering a more complex distribution of particles across multiple energy states.

Let $A$ and $B$ be non-empty finite subsets of integers with the property that $|A| = |B|$. This allows us to define the minimum sumset $|A+B|_{\min}$ as the smallest possible size of the sumset $\{|a+b|: a\in A, b\in B, a\neq -b\}$, where subsets $A$ and $B$ are required to be disjoint from each other's additive inverses. This paper characterizes the structural properties of such non-negative subsets $A$ and $B$ that achieve the minimum sumset $|A+B|_{\min} = (|A| - 1) + |A|$. These characteristics are relevant to both the classic theory of sumsets and that of restricted sums. Building on this, this study also establishes both direct and inverse outcomes of the equation $|A\dot{-} (B-B)| = (|A|-1) + |B|$. This research extends previous findings from prior research articles.

Histopathological examination is a crucial diagnostic tool used in identifying and determining the nature of tumors with the support of a pathological report. Although detecting tumors via histopathological analysis can be accomplished manually, this process is time-consuming and laborious, with the procedure being significantly accelerated with the aid of artificial intelligence systems. These systems require a substantial amount of annotated data for effective training, however, publicly available datasets are often limited in scope and size. In this context, introducing a comprehensive dataset of 14,453 annotated histopathological images from various sources, specifically designed for the classification of colorectal polyps into normal, adenomatous, and carcinomatous categories. Furthermore, this project also involved the development of a tool for training classification models, with the goal of expanding the size of available datasets and enhancing performance metrics.

A novel, locally scaled finite element method is designed to address acoustic scattering issues characterized by varying coefficients, with the analysis taking place in two and three-dimensional spaces. Initially, a standard error estimation technique is reviewed, identifying its limitations in efficiently managing large frequency factors in the scattering problem. This leads to the development of an innovative, frequency-dependent tolerance system, enabling automatic adjustment of mesh refinement and polynomial degree increases/ reductions in response to frequency variations. Consequently, a high-frequency solution can be achieved using refined meshes suitable for lower frequencies, whereas a coarser mesh is adequate for handling smaller frequency scenarios.

A mid-to-late stage of planet formation is hypothesized to involve the growth of planets through the accumulation of small celestial bodies in a relatively calm, inward-moving process. This theory is supported by isotopic evidence from the Chelyabinsk meteorite and a Madagascar meteorite called Benenitra. Both specimens contain chondrules that display distinctive spinel properties, indicating formation under high-pressure conditions. Furthermore, their respective age determinations suggest they arose from the same process at a specific time frame. To explore this hypothesis, a computer simulation was conducted using the Benenitra's age as a reference point. This simulation revealed that, under conditions of low dust density, there exists a specific range where some celestial bodies could form before others, including the Benenitra and Chelyabinsk meteorites, were created. However, in a higher density environment, only lower pressure conditions were produced under those circumstances.

Using the algebraic Bethe-ansatz method, we calculate the fundamental components of the higher-spin XXZ chain's transfer matrix within the affine quantum-group framework. This approach holds true for any excitation level and considers the model's affine quantum-group symmetry, specifically Uq^aff(U(2)). By examining the transfer matrix's affine quantum-group symmetry, we can understand its behavior under various algebraic transformations, which helps us learn about its eigenvalues and the corresponding densities. These higher-spin results can be applied to the affine quantum-group's representation theory at p-adic places, which is relevant to the Reshetikhin-Terada scalar product and the Gaudin-Mehta dihedral symmetry of the XXZ chain's local spin operators.

This paper introduces a novel concept called zero-shot voice translation, which enables the translation of any spoken language into any other language without necessitating a matching language pair. In a surprising finding, we discovered that existing models can achieve meaningful cross-lingual translation without any prior exposure to the involved language pairs. Building on this discovery, we developed a new approach called universal voice translation, which tailors a single model to produce output that adheres to the acoustic characteristics of the language being translated. We surpassed the previous record for the challenging task of voice translation by a significant margin of 5 dB on the most difficult dataset.

We introduce a general technique for estimating the scattering characteristics and optical force experienced by an object in interaction with electromagnetic waves based on the 3D computation of its boundary polarizabilities across multiple frequencies and multipoles. This approach overcomes the limitations of standard approximations used when the incident wavelength is significantly larger than the object's size. While conventional methods, such as the Mie series for spherical objects, provide precise results, many practical applications involve irregularly shaped objects. Our proposed framework utilizes an iterative method, specifically Modified Method of Sources, to compute both the scattering and optical force, with the accuracy determined by the density of the source distribution. Either a uniform or adaptive source placement can be employed. The resulting data enables a detailed examination of how the scattering cross-section and optical force vary with wavelength, as opposed to just examining specific spectral resonance points. This capability is crucial for the effective design of nanostructures for optical manipulation. While our method is illustrated with a spherical object for ease of comparison with the Mie series, its applicability extends to a wide range of object geometries.

This study introduces the concept of Schur shifted symmetric expressions and connects it to quantum Schur polynomials, along with their capital variants. Additionally, we define expressions related to double Young-Capelli bitableaux and link them to the Schur expressions.

In this study, we examine a basic version of the scoto-seesaw model that includes two notable features: neutrino mass generation via the inverse seesaw mechanism and the identification of a WIMP as dark matter. By utilizing effective field theory at the electroweak scale, we simplify the four-neutrino sector to the three-neutrino sector and establish constraints on neutrino oscillation parameters. Furthermore, we demonstrate how the parameter space of the model is limited by neutrino oscillation data, ensuring consistency with experimental observations. In addition, we investigate the conditions under which the Higgs potential remains stable until a high energy scale, providing a link between dark matter, neutrino physics, and the early universe's evolution.
The concept of orbitally mixed states, where adjacent orbitals are merged, is highly relevant for transition metals in their higher oxidation states.

This research extends the concept of quantum Kähler geometry to quantized projective varieties using twisted coherent sheaves as a bridge. By establishing a formal deformation of the algebraic Mumford bundle, we create a relative framework for $\mathbb{A}$-Mumford bundles over families of weighted homogeneous varieties. This allows for the study of relative quantum flag manifolds and their Tannakian reconstruction from relative Weyl algebras, highlighting the preservation of Tannakian structures under Birkhoff transformations through deformed Beilinson-Bernstein equivalence.

As deep learning techniques advance, there is increasing concern about their deployment in medical diagnostics due to the potential for learned biases to influence accuracy. A crucial challenge lies in accurately teaching convolutional neural networks to correctly identify and locate diseases in medical images. This study explores whether garbage filters can be utilized to locate and mark pathological regions in chest X-rays. We developed a dataset and assessed multiple GAN-based models, discovering that they consistently identified disease regions more effectively than random chance across six conditions, outperforming even carefully crafted hand-drawn annotations in three instances. Furthermore, the experiment demonstrated that certain ganFilter models achieved superior performance when tested for their ability to locate disease regions compared to a vast array of hand-crafted disease masks.

ViDaExpert is an advanced graphical interface for exploring and analyzing multidimensional vector fields in 3D. It enables a diverse range of visualization and explanation techniques, including but not limited to stream surfaces, particle tracing, and coherent moving paths. Additionally, the system incorporates an artificial intelligence-driven method for identifying explainable patterns in complex data sets. Built with Python and utilizing the PyQt4 graphical library, ViDaExpert is designed to be easily adaptable and integratable with other scientific modules via Python's import functionality.

This paper proposes a rapid evaluation method for calculating Newtonian potentials within complex two-dimensional regions based on scalar height functions. The proposed approach is particularly useful in various applications, such as solving Laplace's and Poisson's equations, volume rendering, and image registration. We've tested our method using multiple two-dimensional shapes and found that employing a grid leads to a significant speed increase compared to direct calculation.
